brief:
Tonight is Legs A, and it is your first leg session since 20 August. Every weight and every rep on your cards is exactly what you saw yesterday. Nothing has been logged since Pull A on Friday 28 August — that is five days off — and numbers that move without new evidence are just noise, so nothing moved. Leg press opens at 200 and tops at 240. Everything else holds its weight and asks for one more rep than 20 August gave you.

You should know that only two of your three trainers ran this morning. The progression trainer and the recovery trainer both reported, read the same nine lifts, and agreed on every one of them — no disagreements for me to settle and no objections raised. The program trainer, the one that looks at how the whole week is balanced, failed to start three times and never reported. That means no new program suggestion came from it today. It does not affect a single number on your cards, and the five cards already waiting on your phone are carried forward unchanged.

Those five are still waiting and none has been answered since 28 August: leg curl reps on Legs A, cable crunch reps on both leg days, the incline curl going to two sets on Pull B, and face pulls on Pull A going from three sets to two. That last one is your own question from 28 August, put on a card so you can answer it with one tap.

After five days off, treat the first set of leg press as your warm-up read rather than a test. If 200 for ten moves easily, the rest of the night is honest. Get some easy cardio in either today or tomorrow.

Still open and still not something I can put on a card: there is no anti-rotation core movement anywhere in the app's exercise list, so the corrective work you asked about on 17 August cannot be prescribed until that list itself changes. And I still do not know whether Push A on 27 August ran short because of the clock or your legs. Tell me and I will use it.

flags.note: Nothing has been logged since Pull A on 28 August, so every weight and rep tonight is identical to yesterday's review — no new session, no new numbers.
Five days off since 28 August, and this is your first leg session since 20 August. The loads are held, not raised, because of it.

Only two of three trainers ran this morning. Progression and recovery both reported and agreed on all nine lifts; the program trainer failed to start three times and did not report, so no new program suggestion came from it today. No number was affected.

Five cards are waiting for a tap and none has been answered since 28 August: leg curl reps on Legs A, cable crunch reps on both leg days, incline curl to two sets on Pull B, and face pulls on Pull A to two sets.

Still open, and still not something I can put on a card: there is no anti-rotation core movement anywhere in the app's exercise list, so the corrective work you asked about on 17 August cannot be prescribed until that list is changed. Say the word and it gets added.

Push A on 27 August ran 37 minutes and ended after one set of overhead triceps, against 56 minutes for the same session on 17 August — no number has been changed because of it, and I still would like to know whether that was the clock or your legs.
Meso 2, week 2 of 4, a build block — this is the part of the cycle where work goes on, not off.

proposals.why: Your leg curl asks twelve to fifteen reps on Legs A but ten to twelve on Legs B, and it is the same machine at the same 142.5 on both — on 20 August your top Legs A sets were 142.5 for thirteen and thirteen, inside the range but never the top, so the weight can never move, while the identical 142.5 for twelve on Legs B on 16 August is the top of its range and earns the next step; this makes Legs A ten to twelve so the only hamstring work on that day can actually progress.

The cable crunch asks twelve to fifteen and you finished all three sets at thirteen on Legs A and all three at twelve on Legs B, both at 60 — and that machine has no small plate, so its next step is 65 and you can never reach it from inside this range; unlike the hanging leg raise, which carries no weight and needs the high range you accepted, this one is loaded, so ten to twelve makes the twelves you already do earn the next step.

Same change on the other leg day, and they belong together — the Legs B cable crunch sits at the same 60 and finished at twelve on 16 August, so leaving it at twelve to fifteen would freeze it on one day while the other one climbs.

Your last four Pull B nights ran the incline curl at 25 for ten, ten and then eight on 21 July and nine on 28 July, 15 August and 25 August — the first two sets hit the top of the range every single time and only the third one falls short, which is the one thing stopping this slot from ever moving; this makes it two sets, the same fix you accepted on the rope pushdown.

You asked on 28 August why Pull A calls for three face pull sets when you think two is right, and you did two that night — Pull B already runs two, so this makes the two days agree with each other and with you.

overrides.reason: You finished ten reps at 180 last time, which is the top of the range, and 200 is the smallest step this machine makes; the top set stays at 240, the ceiling both trainers who ran today agreed on.
The weight stays at 17.5 because nine, nine and eight never reached the top of the range and the next dumbbell up is 20, which is too big a jump to have earned.

On 20 August you finished fifteen at 127.5, the top of the range, then held thirteen twice at 142.5 — topping the opener is what moves the whole slot to 142.5 tonight instead of starting light again. The fourth set is the one you accepted on 23 August; my recovery trainer withdrew its objection to it on 1 September and did not reopen it today.
Both sets stopped at thirteen inside a twelve to fifteen range, so tonight asks for the reps before it asks for more weight.
Twelve and twelve is the floor of the range, so this steps by one rep at the same weight.
Thirteen and thirteen sits mid-range, so one more rep each; fifteens are what buy the next step up.
Three sets, not four, and one more rep on each at the same 300 — the next pin on this machine is 320 and that is too big a jump from thirteen, thirteen and twelve.

Three flat thirteens with no drop-off on the last set, so this asks fourteen. This machine has no small plate — it steps in fives, so the next real weight is 65 and it waits until you are finishing fifteens.
Bodyweight, so the ask is reps only: you got thirteen then twelve on 20 August, so tonight is thirteen and thirteen.
